COST.name: Costco Wholesale
COST.data_note: Based on SEC filings up to the FY2025 10-K (fiscal year ended 2025-08-31). Later quarters were not reviewed.
COST.summary: Costco deliberately sells at thin margins and earns its profit from membership fees: $5.3B of fees were 51% of FY2025 operating income. Members renew at 92.3% in the US and Canada, and the September 2024 fee increase passed without hurting renewals. The moat is customer loyalty and purchasing scale, not high prices, so the risks are a retail price war, tariffs and labour costs.

evidence.text: Filing names Walmart, Target, Kroger and Amazon as significant competitors, plus Sam's Club and BJ's in warehouse clubs, and calls the industry highly competitive on price, quality and selection.
Operating margin held in a 3.3% to 3.8% band: FY2021 3.4%, FY2022 3.4%, FY2023 3.3%, FY2024 3.6%, FY2025 3.8%.

source.title: SEC XBRL OperatingIncomeLoss and revenue series, CIK 909832

evidence.text: Renewal rate was 92.3% in the US and Canada and 89.8% worldwide at the end of 2025; paid members rose from 71.0M to 81.0M in two years.
The fee increase effective September 1, 2024 accounted for roughly 40% of membership income growth in 2025, with renewal rates still above 90% in the US and Canada.
Filing: Costco does not obtain a significant portion of merchandise from any one supplier.
Gross margin on net sales rose from 10.57% (FY2023) to 10.92% (FY2024) and 11.12% (FY2025) despite tariff exposure the filing describes.
914 warehouses with 134.7M square feet of operating floor space (861 warehouses in FY2023).

source.title: SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss and StockholdersEquity series, CIK 909832

evidence.text: Digitally enabled sales were about 10% of net sales in 2025 and e-commerce comparable sales grew 16%; Amazon is a named competitor.
Filing: higher tariffs could adversely impact results; competitors compete vigorously on price.

supporting.text: Membership fee revenue of $5,323M in FY2025 (up from $4,580M in FY2023) is 51.3% of operating income.
Operating income rose 54.8% from $6,708M (FY2021) to $10,383M (FY2025) while revenue rose 40.5%.

source.title: SEC XBRL OperatingIncomeLoss and revenue series, CIK 909832

supporting.text: Gross margin expanded from 10.57% to 11.12% in two years.

counter.text: About half of operating income comes from membership fees, so profit depends on renewal rates staying above 90%.
SG&A rose from 9.08% to 9.25% of net sales in two years; the filing flags labour, benefit and healthcare costs.
The September 2024 fee increase drove roughly 40% of 2025 membership income growth, a one-time lift that will not repeat annually.

falsifiers.threshold: US and Canada renewal rate below 90%

falsifiers.text: Price war or tariffs squeeze merchandise margin.
falsifiers.threshold: Gross margin on net sales below 10.5%
Paid member growth below 3% a year

tests.name: 2021 to 2023 margin change versus peers
tests.result: Operating margin 3.4% to 3.3%, flat through the 2022 inflation shock. Peer margins (Walmart, Target) were not retrieved, so this test is incomplete.

tests.name: Margin volatility FY2021 to FY2025
tests.result: Range 3.3% to 3.8%. Very low volatility.

tests.name: Price, volume, mix split
tests.result: Not disclosed. Revenue grew 8.2% in FY2025; membership fees grew 10.3%, helped by the fee increase.

LIN.name: Linde plc
LIN.data_note: Based on SEC filings up to the FY2025 10-K (fiscal year ended 2025-12-31). Later quarters were not reviewed.
LIN.summary: Linde sells industrial gases mostly under 10 to 20 year contracts with minimum purchase terms and energy cost pass-through, which locks in volume and protects margin. Operating margin rose from 16.2% in 2021 to 26.3% in 2025 on almost flat sales, which is the signature of pricing power rather than growth. The risks are a slow top line, heavy capex and hydrogen demand that may not arrive on schedule.

evidence.text: Competitors named: Air Liquide, Air Products, Messer and Taiyo Nippon Sanso, plus many small local independents. Basis of competition includes price, reliability and local distribution density.
Operating margin (operating income / sales): 2021 16.2%, 2022 16.1%, 2023 24.4%, 2024 26.2%, 2025 26.3%, while sales rose only 1.9% from 2022 to 2025.
On-site contracts run 10 to 20 years with minimum purchase requirements and price escalation provisions; merchant contracts run three to seven years.
The filing states Linde is not dependent on a single customer or a few customers.
Energy is the single largest cost; electricity, natural gas and diesel costs are mitigated contractually through pricing formulas, surcharges and cost pass-through.

source.title: Linde FY2025 10-K, Item 1 Raw materials and energy

evidence.text: Cost of sales excluding depreciation was 51.2% of sales in 2025 versus 51.9% in 2024 ($17,389M and $17,143M).
2025 capital expenditures were $5,261M, 15.5% of sales; production plants and pipeline networks require high capital and give Linde an advantage where pipelines exist.
Return on ending equity: 2021 8.7%, 2022 10.4%, 2023 15.6%, 2024 17.2%, 2025 18.0% (equity base shrank from $44.0B to $38.2B).

source.title: SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss and StockholdersEquity series, CIK 1707925

evidence.text: A significant portion of the international gases market relates to customer-owned plants, so some buyers can self-supply.
Linde itself sells VPSA and membrane technology that produce oxygen and nitrogen on site, so on-site generation is a partial substitute it also profits from.

supporting.text: Majority of business is under long-term contracts that give cash-flow stability and pass through energy and feedstock costs.
Operating income rose 66.2% from $5,369M (2022) to $8,923M (2025) on sales up 1.9%.
Americas segment operating margin was 31.2% in 2025 ($4,747M on $15,208M sales).

counter.text: Sales grew only 1.9% in three years ($33,364M in 2022 to $33,986M in 2025); margin expansion cannot continue indefinitely.
Equity fell from $49.1B (2019) to $38.2B (2025), so return on equity is flattered by a shrinking base.

source.title: SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss and StockholdersEquity series, CIK 1707925

counter.text: Capex of $5,261M is 15.5% of sales; clean hydrogen growth is described as anticipated, not contracted at scale.

falsifiers.text: Pricing power fades and margin drops.
falsifiers.threshold: Operating margin below 22% for two consecutive fiscal years
Cost of sales excluding depreciation above 55% of sales

falsifiers.text: Returns on the capex programme disappoint.
falsifiers.threshold: Return on ending equity below 12%

tests.name: 2021 to 2023 margin change versus peers
tests.result: Linde operating margin rose 8.2 points (16.2% to 24.4%). Peer margins (Air Liquide, Air Products) were not retrieved in this pass, so this test is not complete.

tests.name: Margin volatility 2021 to 2025
tests.result: Steady upward path: 16.2%, 16.1%, 24.4%, 26.2%, 26.3%. The 2022 to 2023 step was not decomposed; its cause was not verified.

tests.name: Return on ending equity persistence
tests.result: Rising each year from 8.7% to 18.0%.

tests.name: Price, volume, mix split
tests.result: Not retrieved. Sales were flat while margin rose, which fits pricing or mix, but this is inference.

MSFT.name: Microsoft
MSFT.data_note: Financial series run to the fiscal year ended 2026-06-30. Qualitative evidence is from the FY2025 10-K (fiscal year ended 2025-06-30); the FY2026 10-K text was not reviewed.
MSFT.summary: Microsoft's pricing power comes from switching costs: multi-year enterprise agreements and workflows built around Office and Azure. Margins prove it, with operating margin up from 41.6% to 46.8% across five years of 15% plus growth. The weak spots are physical supply (limited GPU and datacenter component suppliers), a dependency on OpenAI, and AI-first rivals that the filing says face low barriers in many areas.

evidence.text: Filing: Azure faces diverse competition from cloud providers and open source; AI offerings compete with hyperscalers and emerging competitors.
Operating margin rose each year from FY2022: 42.1%, 41.8%, 44.6%, 45.6%, 46.8% (FY2026) despite this competition.

source.title: SEC XBRL OperatingIncomeLoss and revenue series, CIK 789019

evidence.text: Enterprise Agreements license products organisation-wide over a three-year period; users may incur costs to move data and buy new content when switching platforms.
Gross margin held in a 68.4% to 69.8% band from FY2021 to FY2025 while revenue grew 68%.
Filing: there are limited suppliers for certain device and datacenter components; datacenters depend on land, energy, networking supplies and servers including GPUs.
Filing names OpenAI as a strategic partner developing AI that Microsoft relies on; a third phase of the partnership was announced in January 2023.
Filing: the company spends substantial amounts to build, purchase or lease datacenters; its cloud benefits from economies of scale and ecosystem network effects.
Filing also says barriers to entry in many of its businesses are low and the areas evolve rapidly.
Filing: AI is a highly competitive and rapidly evolving market with new entrants; Office competes with AI-first application companies.
Filing: open source products at little or no cost mimic features of Microsoft products; mobile devices take over tasks once done on PCs.

supporting.text: Revenue grew from $168.1B (FY2021) to $331.8B (FY2026), 15% to 18% a year in four of five years.
Operating income of $155.2B in FY2026 is 46.8% of revenue, the highest in the series.

source.title: SEC XBRL OperatingIncomeLoss and revenue series, CIK 789019

supporting.text: No single customer is disclosed above 10% of revenue.

counter.text: Return on ending equity fell from 43.2% (FY2021) to 30.2% (FY2026) as equity grew from $142.0B to $442.4B.

source.title: SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss and StockholdersEquity series, CIK 789019

counter.text: FY2026 net income grew 31.3% against operating income growth of 20.8%; the source of the gap (non-operating items) was not verified in this pass.

source.title: SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss and StockholdersEquity series, CIK 789019

counter.text: Filing: government agencies closely scrutinise Microsoft under competition laws, including the EU Digital Markets Act.

falsifiers.text: Cloud and AI competition compresses margins.
falsifiers.threshold: Operating margin below 40% for two consecutive fiscal years

falsifiers.text: Growth stalls as AI substitutes seat-based software.
falsifiers.threshold: Annual revenue growth below 8%
Return on ending equity below 25%

tests.name: 2021 to 2023 margin change versus peers
tests.result: Operating margin 41.6% to 41.8%, stable through the 2022 to 2023 software slowdown. Peer margins (Alphabet, Amazon, Oracle) were not retrieved, so this test is incomplete.

tests.name: Margin volatility FY2021 to FY2026
tests.result: Range 41.6% to 46.8%, low volatility with an upward drift.

tests.name: Return on ending equity persistence
tests.result: 43.2%, 43.7%, 35.1%, 32.8%, 29.6%, 30.2%. Still high but lower; equity base tripled.

tests.name: Price, volume, mix split
tests.result: Not disclosed in the sections reviewed.

MU.name: Micron Technology
MU.data_note: Based on SEC filings up to the FY2025 10-K (fiscal year ended 2025-08-28). Later quarters were not reviewed.
MU.summary: Micron sits in a three-player DRAM oligopoly with huge capital barriers, which reads as strong pricing power. The numbers disagree: gross margin went from 45.2% in FY2022 to -9.1% in FY2023 and back to 39.8% in FY2025, so Micron takes the cycle's price rather than setting it. HBM is the new lever, but the filing itself warns that a demand shift could flood conventional DRAM.

evidence.text: The 10-K names Samsung, SK hynix, Kioxia, Sandisk, CXMT and YMTC as competitors, and notes government assistance to CXMT and YMTC.
Gross margin (gross profit / revenue): FY2021 37.6%, FY2022 45.2%, FY2023 -9.1%, FY2024 22.4%, FY2025 39.8%.

source.title: SEC XBRL GrossProfit and Revenue series, CIK 723125

evidence.text: Filing: in some prior periods average selling prices were below manufacturing costs.

source.title: Micron FY2025 10-K, Item 1A volatility in ASP

evidence.text: Approximately one-half of total revenue came from the top ten customers in each of the last three years.

source.title: Micron FY2025 10-K, Item 1 Marketing and Customers

evidence.text: Revenue fell 49.5% from $30.758B (FY2022) to $15.540B (FY2023), then rose to $37.378B in FY2025, so volume and price follow the market, not Micron.
Only a limited number of suppliers can deliver certain materials, in some cases single or sole source; certain materials come predominantly from China.
Supply chain depends on third-party controller makers and outsourced foundries, assembly and test providers.
Semiconductor manufacturing is capital intensive; fabs are complex projects needing specialised skills, and fab building has been uncommon in recent years.

source.title: Micron FY2025 10-K, Item 1 Manufacturing and Item 1A

evidence.text: Return on ending equity: FY2021 13.3%, FY2022 17.4%, FY2023 -13.2%, FY2024 1.7%, FY2025 15.8%. Entry is hard but returns are not persistent.

source.title: SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss and StockholdersEquity series, CIK 723125

evidence.text: State-backed CXMT and YMTC are named as government-assisted competitors, which weakens the capital barrier.
Competitors are developing new memory and storage technologies that may offer performance or cost advantages and render existing technologies obsolete.
Volume production of 8-high 24GB HBM3E began in 2024; the filing warns that a shift of capacity away from HBM could significantly raise conventional DRAM supply.

supporting.text: Three-player DRAM oligopoly with very high fab capital needs; fab building has been uncommon in recent years.
FY2025 revenue of $37.378B and operating income of $9.770B (26.1% margin) are the strongest in the series.

source.title: SEC XBRL OperatingIncomeLoss and revenue series, CIK 723125

supporting.text: HBM3E volume production started in 2024, a higher-value product line.

counter.text: FY2023 operating loss of $5.745B on $15.540B revenue (-37.0% margin) shows the oligopoly did not protect margins in a downturn.
Filing: annual DRAM ASP changes have ranged from about +40% to -40%, so price is set by the market.
Filing: China's CAC barred critical information infrastructure operators from buying Micron products (May 2023), and a majority of 2025 DRAM output came from Taiwan fabs.

falsifiers.text: Gross margin collapses as in the last downturn.
falsifiers.threshold: Gross margin below 30% for two consecutive quarters

falsifiers.text: HBM demand weakens and capacity shifts to conventional DRAM.
falsifiers.threshold: DRAM average selling price down more than 20% year on year
Top ten customers above 60% of revenue

tests.name: 2021 to 2023 operating margin change
tests.result: 22.7% to -37.0%, a 59.7 point fall. Peer figures (Samsung, SK hynix) are not SEC filers and were not retrieved, so no peer comparison.

tests.name: Margin volatility FY2021 to FY2025
tests.result: Operating margin 22.7%, 31.5%, -37.0%, 5.2%, 26.1%. Very high.

reconciliation.story: Oligopoly structure and capital barriers suggest durable pricing power.
reconciliation.numbers: Gross margin swung from 45.2% to -9.1% to 39.8% within three years, and return on equity turned negative in FY2023.

V.name: Visa
V.data_note: Based on SEC filings up to the FY2025 10-K (fiscal year ended 2025-09-30). FY2021 data and later quarters were not reviewed. Financial figures come from the two earnings releases above; the 10-K was read for business and risk text only.
V.summary: Visa is a two-sided network with 14,500 financial institutions and over 175 million merchant locations, so every extra participant makes it harder to replace. GAAP operating margin has held at 60% to 66% and return on equity has climbed past 50%. The pressure points are client incentives, now 28% of gross revenue and growing faster than revenue, and regulators and real-time payment systems attacking the fee.

evidence.text: Filing compares Visa's $15.9T total volume and 311B transactions with Mastercard's $8.0T and 204B, and American Express's $1.8T and 12B.
GAAP operating margin: FY2022 64.2%, FY2023 64.3%, FY2024 65.7%, FY2025 60.0% (litigation provision of $2.562B vs $462M).

source.title: Visa Q4 FY2025 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)

evidence.text: Client incentives were $15,751M in FY2025 (+14%) against net revenue growth of 11%; as a share of gross revenue they rose from 27.7% to 28.3%.

source.title: Visa Q4 FY2025 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)

evidence.text: Filing: governments use regulation to drive down merchant discount rates; interchange caps exist in the EU (20 and 30 bps), Australia, New Zealand and Latin America; Credit Card Competition Act may be reintroduced.
Filing identifies four global data centers and telecommunications infrastructure as critical; no vendor concentration is disclosed.
Personnel expense of $6.961B in FY2025 was the main non-litigation cost and no input supplier is described as a constraint.

source.title: Visa Q4 FY2025 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)

evidence.text: Scale: nearly 14,500 financial institutions, more than 175 million merchant locations, about 12 billion cards, accounts and wallets, 329 billion transactions in fiscal 2025.
Return on ending equity: FY2022 42.0%, FY2023 44.6%, FY2024 50.4%, FY2025 52.9%.

source.title: Visa Q4 FY2025 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)

evidence.text: Filing: real-time payment networks have launched in at least 80 countries with strong government sponsorship (FedNow, PIX, UPI) and can compete on consumer, B2B and P2P payments.
Filing cites stablecoins, account-to-account payments, BNPL and cash and checks as competing forms of payment.

supporting.text: Net revenue grew 11.4%, 10.0% and 11.3% in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 ($32.7B to $40.0B).

source.title: Visa Q4 FY2025 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)

supporting.text: Non-GAAP net income rose 11% to $22.5B in FY2025, excluding litigation and other special items.

source.title: Visa Q4 FY2025 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)

supporting.text: Payments volume +8%, cross-border volume +13% and processed transactions +10% in FY2025.

source.title: Visa Q4 FY2025 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)

counter.text: GAAP operating income grew only 2% in FY2025 ($23,994M vs $23,595M) because the litigation provision rose to $2.562B from $462M.

source.title: Visa Q4 FY2025 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)

counter.text: Client incentives grew 14% in FY2025, faster than net revenue (11%), a sign issuers and merchants capture more of the economics.

source.title: Visa Q4 FY2025 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)

counter.text: A District Court ruling in August 2025 vacated the Federal Reserve debit fee standard, and new interchange caps keep appearing (New Zealand cross-border caps adopted July 2025).

falsifiers.threshold: Client incentives above 30% of gross revenue
Non-GAAP operating margin below 60% or GAAP below 55%

falsifiers.text: Volume growth slows as substitutes gain share.
falsifiers.threshold: Payments volume growth below 5%

tests.name: 2021 to 2023 margin change versus peers
tests.result: FY2022 to FY2023 GAAP operating margin 64.2% to 64.3%, flat. FY2021 and peer (Mastercard) figures were not retrieved, so this test is incomplete.

tests.name: Margin volatility FY2022 to FY2025
tests.result: 64.2%, 64.3%, 65.7%, 60.0%. The FY2025 dip is attributed to the litigation provision, not pricing.

tests.name: Return on ending equity persistence
tests.result: 42.0%, 44.6%, 50.4%, 52.9%. Rising; helped by buybacks (equity fell from $39.1B to $37.9B in FY2025).

tests.name: Price, volume, mix split
tests.result: Volume-driven: payments volume +8%, processed transactions +10%, revenue +11%. No pure price split disclosed in sections reviewed.

GOOGL.name: Alphabet
GOOGL.data_note: Based on the FY2025 10-K (year ended 2025-12-31). Later quarters were not reviewed. 2022 revenue was not available under the same XBRL tag, so 2022 is omitted.
GOOGL.summary: Alphabet earns a steady 32% operating margin on a very wide base of advertisers, and returns on equity are above 30%. The weak force is substitutes: the company itself flags generative AI as a way users may bypass its products, and a December 2025 US court judgment limits how search is distributed. Those risks have not yet shown up in the numbers.

evidence.text: Filing lists competitors across search engines, e-commerce, ad networks, cloud providers, AI model developers, hardware makers, video and social networks.

source.title: SEC XBRL OperatingIncomeLoss and Revenues, CIK 1652044

evidence.text: Revenue grew 15.1% in 2025, from $350.018B to $402.836B.
Filing: over 70% of 2025 revenue came from online advertising, sold to a very large base of advertisers and delivered across Search, YouTube and Network partners.
Operating margin stayed between 32.0% and 32.1% in 2024 and 2025 while revenue grew 15.1%, so advertisers did not extract price concessions. Single-customer concentration was not retrieved.

source.title: SEC XBRL OperatingIncomeLoss and Revenues, CIK 1652044

evidence.text: Filing: operations depend on TPUs (custom, seventh generation Ironwood), specialised GPUs, a limited set of server and networking suppliers, energy and data centre capacity.
Filing: extended or unforeseen disruptions at these suppliers could affect the ability to meet customer demand.
Filing names AI model developers and providers of AI products and services as competitors, alongside large incumbents and emerging startups.

source.title: SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss and StockholdersEquity, CIK 1652044

evidence.text: Filing: generative AI is changing how users obtain information online, potentially reducing the utility of existing products and services.

Filing: the December 2025 final judgment in the US search case restricts how Alphabet distributes its services and requires sharing certain search data and offering syndication to certain competitors.
Filing: April 2025 ad tech ruling found publisher tools unfairly excluded rivals; DOJ proposed structural remedies and a remedies decision is pending.

supporting.text: 2025 revenue $402.836B, operating income $129.039B (32.0% margin), net income $132.170B.

source.title: SEC XBRL Revenues, OperatingIncomeLoss, NetIncomeLoss, CIK 1652044

supporting.text: Operating income grew 14.8% in 2025 on revenue growth of 15.1%, so margin held.

source.title: SEC XBRL OperatingIncomeLoss and Revenues, CIK 1652044

supporting.text: Return on ending equity rose from 26.0% (2023) to 31.8% (2025).

source.title: SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss and StockholdersEquity, CIK 1652044

counter.text: Over 70% of revenue is advertising, so one profit pool carries the business.
The December 2025 search judgment limits distribution deals and forces data sharing and syndication to competitors.
Generative AI is named by the company as a way users may get information outside its products.

falsifiers.threshold: Revenue growth below 8% year on year for two consecutive quarters
Operating margin below 28% for two consecutive quarters
Court orders divestiture of ad exchange or publisher ad server

tests.name: Operating margin 2023 to 2025
tests.result: 27.4%, 32.1%, 32.0%. Held after the 2024 step up.

tests.name: Return on ending equity
tests.result: 26.0%, 30.8%, 31.8%. Rising with a growing equity base.

tests.name: Margin change vs peers
tests.result: Not completed. Peer filings (Microsoft, Meta) were not retrieved for this card.

reconciliation.story: Scale and distribution give strong pricing power, but legal remedies and generative AI threaten the search franchise.
reconciliation.numbers: Margins and returns are strong and stable, so the threats are not yet in the numbers; the risk is forward looking.

AMZN.name: Amazon
AMZN.data_note: Based on the FY2025 10-K (year ended 2025-12-31) and the Q4 2025 results release for segment data. Segment figures come from the release, not the 10-K text. Customer concentration was not retrieved.
AMZN.summary: Amazon's group operating margin rose from 2.4% in 2022 to 11.2% in 2025, but one segment carries it: AWS earned 57% of operating income on 18% of revenue. Retail competes in an intensely competitive market at a 6.9% North America margin. 2025 capital spending of $131.8B exceeded operating income, so the cloud thesis has to keep paying.

evidence.text: Filing: businesses are rapidly evolving and intensely competitive, with many competitors across geographies and industries including retailers, cloud providers, media, logistics and advertising.
North America segment operating margin was 6.9% in 2025 ($29.6B on $426.3B) against 6.5% in 2024.

source.title: SEC XBRL OperatingIncomeLoss and Revenue, CIK 1018724

evidence.text: AWS operating margin was 35.4% in 2025 ($45.6B on $128.7B), down from 37.0% in 2024, so large cloud buyers have not forced it down sharply.
Retail buyers are millions of consumers and sellers; no single buyer sets terms. Customer concentration figures were not retrieved.
Filing: Amazon relies on a limited group of suppliers for semiconductor products, including GPUs for AI infrastructure.
Capital spending (purchases of property and equipment, net) was $131.8B in 2025, which exceeds 2025 operating income of $79.975B.
AWS net sales were $128.7B in 2025 (+20%) and Q4 growth was 24%; group capital spending was $131.8B in 2025, a scale few entrants can fund.

source.title: SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss and StockholdersEquity, CIK 1018724

evidence.text: Filing: open investigations and litigation on competition and consumer protection, including FTC and state attorneys general suits, cover the stores and certain AWS offerings.
Filing lists web search engines, comparison shopping sites and social networks among competitors for consumer attention.

supporting.text: 2025 revenue $716.924B (+12.4%), operating income $79.975B (11.2% margin), net income $77.670B.

source.title: SEC XBRL Revenue, OperatingIncomeLoss, NetIncomeLoss, CIK 1018724

supporting.text: AWS earned $45.6B of operating income on 18.0% of revenue, 57% of the company total.
Operating margin rose from 2.4% in 2022 to 11.2% in 2025.

source.title: SEC XBRL OperatingIncomeLoss and Revenue, CIK 1018724

counter.text: Retail margin is thin: North America 6.9% and International 2.9% ($4.7B on $161.9B) in 2025.
Capex of $131.8B in 2025 is larger than operating income, so returns depend on AI and cloud demand holding.
AWS margin slipped from 37.0% to 35.4% in 2025.

falsifiers.threshold: AWS operating margin below 30% for two consecutive quarters
Capex above 100% of operating cash flow for a full year
North America operating margin below 5% for two consecutive quarters

tests.name: Operating margin 2022 to 2025
tests.result: 2.4%, 6.4%, 10.8%, 11.2%. Rising and now flattening.

tests.name: Segment mix
tests.result: AWS is 18.0% of revenue and 57% of operating income; the group margin rests on one segment.

tests.name: Margin change vs peers
tests.result: Not completed. Peer filings (Microsoft, Walmart) were not retrieved for this card.

reconciliation.story: Scale in cloud and logistics gives pricing power in cloud, while retail stays intensely competitive.
reconciliation.numbers: Group margin is rising, but retail margins are thin and AWS carries 57% of profit.

JPM.name: JPMorgan Chase
JPM.data_note: Based on the FY2025 10-K (year ended 2025-12-31) and the Q4 2025 earnings release narrative for ROE, ROTCE and CET1. Banks are scored on revenue, net income and capital, not gross margin. Customer concentration was not retrieved.
JPM.summary: JPMorgan has earned 13% to 17% on ending equity for five years with a 14.5% CET1 ratio, and net interest income has risen to $95.4B. The risks are slowing growth (net interest income +3.1% in 2025) and a 33% rise in credit provisions. Capital rules and fintech competition are the named structural threats.

evidence.text: Filing: competitors include banks, brokerages, investment banks, hedge funds, private equity, insurers, asset managers, card companies, e-commerce and digital asset and fintech firms.

source.title: SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss and Revenues, CIK 19617

evidence.text: Revenue grew 2.8% in 2025 ($177.556B to $182.447B), after 12.3% growth in 2024.
Net interest income was $95.443B in 2025, up 3.1% on 2024 and up from $52.311B in 2021, so lending spreads held as rates moved.
Retail, corporate and institutional clients are numerous. Customer concentration figures were not retrieved, so this is a judgment.
Net interest income equals 52.3% of 2025 revenue and has risen every year since 2021.

source.title: SEC XBRL InterestIncomeExpenseNet and Revenues, CIK 19617

evidence.text: Capital is the scarce input: CET1 ratio was 14.5% (Standardized) and 14.1% (Advanced) at 31 December 2025.
Filing: firms offering products solely through internet channels and non-financial companies are named as competitors that may disintermediate traditional banking.
Filing: the Firm is subject to extensive supervision and regulation, including a July 2023 US proposal to revise risk-based capital rules for banks with assets of $100B or more.

source.title: SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss and StockholdersEquity, CIK 19617

evidence.text: Filing names digital asset and other financial technology companies and e-commerce firms among competitors for banking services.
Provision for credit losses rose 33.1% in 2025 to $14.212B (7.8% of revenue) from $10.678B (6.0%).

supporting.text: 2025 net income $57.048B; management reports ROE 17% and ROTCE 20%.

AMT.name: American Tower
AMT.data_note: Based on the FY2025 10-K (year ended 2025-12-31), cross-checked to the Q4 2025 earnings release 8-K. Income statement figures for 2023 to 2025 and balance sheet figures for 2024 and 2025 were retrieved. Customer percentages are shares of total operating revenues as the filing states. Share of sites on leased land, barriers to entry and the floating-rate debt share were not found in the retrieved text. Weak does not apply here; scores reflect pricing power only, not company quality.
AMT.summary: American Tower rents towers to a few large carriers on long leases with a fixed escalator averaging about 3%, and churn was about 2% of billings in 2025. Buyer power is the weak spot: T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon were 49% of 2025 revenue and DISH defaulted in January 2026. Operating margin reached 45.5%, but debt of $37.2B is 359% of equity.

evidence.text: Filing: named competitors are Crown Castle International Corp., SBA Communications Corporation, Vertical Bridge, Telesites S.A.B. de C.V. and Cellnex Telecom, S.A. Market share data was not found in the retrieved text.

Operating income as a share of total operating revenues: 2023 31.2%, 2024 44.6%, 2025 45.5%. The 2023 figure includes $2,928.5M of depreciation, amortization and accretion and a $80.0M goodwill impairment.

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations

evidence.text: Total operating revenues grew 1.1% in 2024 ($10,012.2M to $10,127.2M) and 5.1% in 2025 ($10,644.6M).

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations

evidence.text: Filing: a substantial portion of total operating revenues comes from a small number of customers. 2025 shares of total operating revenues: T-Mobile 18%, AT&T 17%, Verizon Wireless 14%, Telefonica 10%.

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Item 1A Customer concentration

evidence.text: The top three carriers were 51% of total operating revenues in 2023, 50% in 2024 and 49% in 2025. Adding Telefonica, four customers were 59% in 2025.

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Item 1A Customer concentration

evidence.text: Filing: DISH represented approximately 2% of total annual property revenue and 4% of U.S. & Canada property revenue for 2025, and was in default on its Strategic Collocation Agreement as of January 2026.

Filing: churn was approximately 2% of tenant billings in 2025. Leases have initial non-cancellable terms of five to ten years with multiple renewal terms and a fixed escalator averaging approximately 3% in the United States.

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Item 1 Tenant leases

evidence.text: Filing: ground rent is primarily fixed under long-term lease agreements with annual cost escalations. The share of sites on leased land and landlord concentration were not found in the retrieved text.

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Item 1A Ground leases

evidence.text: Property operating expense was $2,501.4M in 2023, $2,481.8M in 2024 and $2,574.1M in 2025, equal to 25.0%, 24.5% and 24.2% of total operating revenues.

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations

evidence.text: Operating income margin of 45.5% in 2025 and 44.6% in 2024 on total operating revenues, with property revenue the dominant line. Management reports a 67.0% Adjusted EBITDA margin for 2025.

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations

evidence.text: Competitors named in the filing are a short list of large tower owners; a barriers-to-entry discussion was not found in the retrieved text, so the score rests on margins and asset scale: property and equipment, net of $20,356.3M.

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Consolidated Balance Sheets

evidence.text: Management reports 2025 Adjusted EBITDA of $7,130M and a 67.0% margin.

source.title: American Tower Q4 and full year 2025 results press release (8-K)

evidence.text: Filing: small cell complementary network technologies or satellite services could shift a portion of customers' network investments away from traditional tower-based networks; DAS networks are named as alternative infrastructure.

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Item 1A Technology risks

evidence.text: Filing: more spectrally efficient technologies could reduce the capacity customers need from towers.

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Item 1A Technology risks

evidence.text: Churn was approximately 2% of tenant billings in 2025, so substitution had not yet shown up materially in lost billings.

supporting.text: Operating income rose 7.3% in 2025 ($4,516.5M to $4,845.8M) on revenue growth of 5.1%; operating margin 45.5%.

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations

supporting.text: Interest expense fell 3.2% in 2025 ($1,404.5M to $1,359.4M) and operating income covered it 3.56 times (2.25 times in 2023).

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations

supporting.text: Net income was $2,628.5M in 2025 against $2,280.2M in 2024 (the 2024 figure includes a $978.3M loss from discontinued operations).

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations

counter.text: Debt of $37,220.3M (current $3,387.8M plus long-term $33,832.5M) is 359% of total equity of $10,355.3M and 58.9% of total assets.

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Consolidated Balance Sheets

counter.text: Three carriers were 49% of total operating revenues in 2025, and DISH was in default as of January 2026.
Other expense was -$576.2M in 2025 against +$377.6M in 2024, pulling pre-tax income down 16.0% ($3,624.8M to $3,044.2M) despite higher operating income. The drivers were not retrieved.

source.title: American Tower FY2025 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations

falsifiers.threshold: Churn above 4% of tenant billings in any full year, or any single customer above 20% of total operating revenues
Operating income divided by interest expense below 3.0 times for a full year
Operating income below 42% of total operating revenues for a full year

tests.name: Operating margin 2023 to 2025
tests.result: 31.2%, 44.6%, 45.5%. The 2023 level reflects heavy depreciation and impairment charges.

tests.name: Revenue and net income cross-check to 8-K
tests.result: Total revenue $10,645M, operating income $4,845.8M, net income $2,628.5M and interest expense $1,359.4M match the 10-K statements.

tests.name: Customer concentration trend
tests.result: Top three share of total operating revenues 51%, 50%, 49% (2023 to 2025). Slowly easing, still high.

tests.name: Margin change vs peers
tests.result: Not completed. Peer filings (Crown Castle, SBA) were not retrieved for this card.

reconciliation.story: Long non-cancellable leases with fixed escalators and a short list of tower peers support stable pricing, but three carriers hold about half of revenue and give buyers leverage.
reconciliation.numbers: Operating margin of 45.5% and 2% churn fit the story; the DISH default and 359% debt to equity show the concentration and leverage risks.
